notes: Sheet is drawn north-up, unlike 162/172 which are rotated ~45 deg; in the lower left the 162 grid appears rotated: Dorsey, Goethe, Seitz and Mulberry come in as NW-SE diagonals from the left edge and each bends to run E across the sheet to Sycamore, and Lang runs SW-NE across them (crosses Goethe, Seitz starts at Lang, Mulberry crossed at the far left) and ends at the Dorsey bend, where its line continues north as Main. Names as printed: DORCHESTER AV., MAIN, AUBURN TERRACE (McILVAINE), EDINBURGH PL., EXCELSIOR, SYCAMORE, ALMA, WALKER, RINGGOLD, DORSEY, GOETHE, SEITZ (MIAMI), MULBERRY, LANG, HUGHES, ANTIQUE (no suffixes); sheet 172 also has streets printed AUBURN TERRACE (SYCAMORE), a different street from this Auburn Terrace. Main: 85 ft printed north of Excelsior (faces x 1093/1387) and 50 ft south of it (east face moves to x~1263); between y~1900 and Dorsey its west line steps in to x~1175. Excelsior's west leg (y~1016, 40 ft) and east leg (y~1181, 50 ft) are offset at Main. Sycamore runs N-S (centre x~2677) from the bottom edge to y~850, then turns ENE (65 ft printed near the bend, 70 ft near Walker) to the top-right corner; it does not reach Dorchester on this sheet. North of the bend a retaining wall (y~705-710) closes off a 25 ft strip (x 2576-2662) that runs up to Dorchester west of lots 133-147; Edinburgh Pl (about 22 ft, y 633-710) runs east from an unnamed 12 ft alley (x~2243) to that strip, on the upper level above the wall, so the strip is recorded as Edinburgh Pl's north leg (it could instead be an unnamed lane or a remnant of old Sycamore). A second unlabelled 14 ft gap (x 2077-2125) runs south from Dorchester to the rear yards (~y 610). Alma (20 ft) runs from Sycamore to the bottom edge, widening to 55 ft at y~4180. Walker (40 ft) runs from Sycamore to the bottom edge; Ringgold comes in from the right edge (y 3726-3901) and ends at Walker (printed vertically in the gap). A stairway (STEPS) runs N-S at x~1237 from Goethe down to Seitz. Seitz diagonal leg measures ~30-40 ft between faces (printed 30'); its points use block lines. Mulberry/Main/Antique is the same 5-way junction as on sheet 156.
